title: The Natural Density of the Non-Three-Square Integers Is 1/6
description: The quantitative capstone of the three-square exceptional family E = {4^a(8b+7)}: the integers that are NOT sums of three squares have natural density exactly 1/6. The proof builds a 4-descent counting recursion excludedCount N = ⌊N/8⌋ + excludedCount ⌈N/4⌉ from the self-similar structure of E, derives an explicit logarithmic error bound by strong induction, and concludes via the standard log N / N → 0. Asymptotically, one integer in six requires all four squares of Lagrange's theorem.

overview.historicalContext: By Legendre's three-square theorem (1798), the integers not representable as x²+y²+z² are exactly the excluded family E = {4^a(8b+7)} — precisely the numbers that require the full four squares in Lagrange's four-square theorem (1770), i.e. the extremal numbers for Waring's problem g(2) = 4. While which integers lie in E is classical, how RARE they are is a natural quantitative question not previously formalized in the gallery. The heuristic answer is a geometric series: the disjoint 2-adic layers 4^a·(8b+7) contribute densities 1/(8·4^a) summing to (1/8)(4/3) = 1/6. Turning this heuristic into a theorem — a rigorous natural-density statement with a controlled error term — is the content of this entry, the quantitative sequel to oq-03-oq-04's structural 2-adic normal form.
overview.problemStatement: Prove that the excluded family E = {4^a(8b+7)} has natural density exactly 1/6: with excludedCount N = #{n < N : n ∈ E}, show excludedCount N / N → 1/6 as N → ∞. Equivalently, the asymptotic proportion of integers that are not sums of three squares (that need all four squares) is one in six.
overview.proofStrategy: Exploit the self-similarity of E. The descent facts (n ≡ 7 mod 8 ⟹ excluded; 4k excluded ⟺ k excluded) split E ∩ [0,N) into the residue class {n ≡ 7 mod 8} (exactly ⌊N/8⌋ elements) and a bijective 1/4-scaled copy of E (via n ↦ n/4), giving the recursion excludedCount N = ⌊N/8⌋ + excludedCount ⌈N/4⌉. Strong induction on this recursion yields the explicit bound |6·excludedCount N − N| ≤ 6(log₂ N + 1): each step perturbs the error by ≤ 6 over a log-depth descent. Dividing by 6N and squeezing with (log₂ N + 1)/N → 0 (from Real.log N / N → 0) gives the density 1/6.
keyInsights: The excluded family is 2-adically self-similar — a residue class plus a 1/4-scaled copy of itself — and that single structural fact reduces the whole density computation to one recursion.

The constant 1/6 = Σ 1/(8·4^a) is the value of a geometric series, but the proof never forms an infinite sum: it is captured as a single inductive invariant (the logarithmic error bound), which is both cleaner and constructively sharper.
The deviation from perfect density is only logarithmic, |6·excludedCount N − N| ≤ 6(log₂ N + 1), so the convergence is fast and the error is explicit — more than the bare density limit requires.

The result quantifies Waring's g(2) = 4: a positive proportion, exactly 1/6, of all integers genuinely need the fourth square; the four-square theorem is not 'almost always' overkill but necessary one-sixth of the time.

The descent-plus-residue method is general: it computes the density of any 2-adically self-similar set as a geometric series plus a logarithmic remainder, and should transfer to the exceptional sets of other ternary quadratic genera.

meta.author: Lean Genius
originalContributions: excludedCount_density: the headline — the excluded family E = {4^a(8b+7)} of Legendre's three-square theorem has NATURAL DENSITY exactly 1/6. Formally, excludedCount N / N → 1/6 as N → ∞, where excludedCount N = #{n < N : n ∈ E}. Equivalently, asymptotically one integer in six is NOT a sum of three squares — i.e. requires the full four squares of Lagrange's theorem (the extremal numbers for Waring's g(2) = 4). No counting or density statement about the three-square exceptional set appears anywhere else in the gallery.

excludedCount_rec: a 4-descent COUNTING RECURSION excludedCount N = N/8 + excludedCount ((N+3)/4). An excluded number below N is either odd and ≡ 7 (mod 8) — there are exactly ⌊N/8⌋ of those (card_mod8_seven) — or divisible by 4 with quotient again excluded, in bijection (n ↦ n/4) with the excluded numbers below ⌈N/4⌉. This self-similar decomposition is the engine of the density computation.

excludedCount_error_bound: an explicit logarithmic error bound |6·excludedCount N − N| ≤ 6·(log₂ N + 1), proved by STRONG INDUCTION directly from the recursion. Each descent step perturbs the error 6·excludedCount N − N by a bounded amount (≤ 6 in absolute value), and the descent depth is log₂-controlled (the (N+3)/4 step at most halves N). This pins the constant 1/6 — which is the sum of the geometric series Σ 1/(8·4^a) = (1/8)(4/3) — WITHOUT ever forming an infinite sum: the bound is a single inductive invariant.
card_mod8_seven: the exact residue count #{n < N : n ≡ 7 (mod 8)} = ⌊N/8⌋, proved by a clean Finset induction matching the divisibility recurrence (N+1)/8 = N/8 + [N ≡ 7 mod 8].

filter_notdvd_eq_mod8 / excludedCount_dvd_part: the two halves of the descent — that the not-divisible-by-4 part of the excluded set is exactly the ≡ 7 (mod 8) residue class, and that the divisible-by-4 part is in explicit bijection (Finset.card_bij' via n ↦ n/4, k ↦ 4k) with a smaller copy of the excluded set, using the multiply-by-4 descent four_mul_excluded_iff (4k ∈ E ⟺ k ∈ E).
prerequisites: IsExcludedForm and its computable Decidable instance from the sibling oq-03-oq-04 entry (the 2-adic normal form), reused so that excludedCount is a genuine Finset.card.
Finset.card_bij' (Mathlib): cardinality via an explicit two-sided bijection — used to match the divisible-by-4 part of the excluded set with a smaller copy of itself.
Finset.filter_card_add_filter_neg_card_eq_card (Mathlib): splits the excluded set into its divisible-by-4 and not-divisible-by-4 parts.
Nat.log API (Mathlib): Nat.log_div_base, Nat.log_mono_right, Nat.log_pos, Nat.pow_log_le_self — control the descent depth for the error bound.

Real.isLittleO_log_id_atTop and Asymptotics.IsLittleO.tendsto_div_nhds_zero (Mathlib): the standard log N / N → 0, combined via squeeze_zero' with the bound (Nat.log 2 N + 1)/N to drive the density limit.

mathlibDependencies.description: Cardinality equality from an explicit bijection with a two-sided inverse; realizes the 4-descent step #{n < N : 4∣n ∧ n∈E} = excludedCount ⌈N/4⌉ via n ↦ n/4.
#(s.filter p) + #(s.filter ¬p) = #s; partitions the excluded set below N by divisibility-by-4.

openQuestions.question: Sharpen the density limit to an explicit error term: prove excludedCount N = N/6 + O(log N) with a named constant, or determine the true order of the oscillation of 6·excludedCount N − N (the inductive bound gives O(log N); is the truth O(1) along subsequences, or genuinely unbounded?).

Compute the natural density of the exceptional sets of the other two-class ternary genera (x²+y²+2z², x²+2y²+2z², etc.) using the same descent-plus-residue method, and compare: do the Waring-extremal densities for related ternary forms also reduce to a single geometric series in the relevant prime?

crossReferences.description: Direct sequel: oq-03-oq-04 supplies the 2-adic normal form, uniqueness of the 4^a(8b+7) parametrisation, and the computable Decidable instance for E; this entry uses that decidability to define the counting function excludedCount and answers oq-03-oq-04's own follow-up question (density 1/6), realizing the geometric-series heuristic stated there as a fully verified limit.

The two-square sufficiency slice studies which non-excluded n are reachable; this entry instead measures the size of the excluded complement, completing the qualitative-plus-quantitative picture of the three-square exceptional set.

conclusion.summary: The quantitative capstone of the three-square exceptional family E = {4^a(8b+7)} — the integers that are NOT sums of three squares (equivalently, that require all four squares of Lagrange's theorem, the extremal numbers for Waring's g(2) = 4). The headline excludedCount_density proves these have natural density exactly 1/6: excludedCount N / N → 1/6, where excludedCount N = #{n < N : n ∈ E}. The proof rests on a 4-descent counting recursion excludedCount N = N/8 + excludedCount ⌈N/4⌉ (excludedCount_rec) — every excluded number below N is either ≡ 7 (mod 8) (exactly ⌊N/8⌋ of them, card_mod8_seven) or 4 times a smaller excluded number (a Finset bijection, excludedCount_dvd_part) — together with an explicit logarithmic error bound |6·excludedCount N − N| ≤ 6·(log₂ N + 1) (excludedCount_error_bound) proved by strong induction. The constant 1/6 is the geometric sum Σ 1/(8·4^a) = (1/8)(4/3), pinned by the inductive invariant rather than by manipulating an infinite series; the limit then follows from the standard log N / N → 0. 305 lines, 12 theorems, 1 definition, 0 axioms, 0 sorries; #print axioms = [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], no native_decide.
conclusion.implications: Where oq-03-oq-04 gave the structural / decidable description of the three-square exceptional set, this entry gives its measure: the non-three-square integers are not merely infinite but have a definite asymptotic frequency, one in six. The descent-plus-residue method is general — it reduces a density computation for a 2-adically self-similar set to a single geometric series and a logarithmic remainder — and is reusable for the exceptional sets of other ternary quadratic genera. The result also quantifies Waring's g(2) = 4: a positive proportion (exactly 1/6) of all integers genuinely need the fourth square.
